reports.title: Nebius reports third quarter 2026 financial results

lines: Today we are updating our guidance for 2026: • With a portion of this year’s revenue moving into the first part of next year, we now expect 2026 revenue at the low end of our $3.0-3.4 billion range, with an adjusted EBITDA margin of ca. 40%. • We now expect the ARR we guided to for December to arrive in February, even before New Jersey ramps up to full capacity.

And we are also sharing our initial outlook for 2027: • We expect to reach pre-tax breakeven by the end of 2027, on the back of the structural benefits discussed above. • We expect revenue of $12-13 billion, reflecting a conservative approach to the pace of our build-out.
We expect $10 billion in committed customer prepayments in 2026, rising to $17 20 billion in 2027.

The contracts behind that capacity remain in place. • Revenue: We now expect revenue at the low end of our $3.0-3.4 billion range. • Adjusted EBITDA margin: Unchanged, at approximately 40%. • Capital expenditures: Approximately $27 billion, above our $20-25 billion range, as we invest in capacity for 2027, in particular at our owned sites. • ARR: We had guided to $7-9 billion by December.

We now expect ARR to exceed $7 billion for the month of February, a shift of about two months, even before New Jersey ramps up to full capacity. • Contracted power: We continue to expect 5 GW of contracted power by year-end, from more than 4 GW today. 2027: initial outlook • • • • • Revenue: $12-13 billion, approximately four times our 2026 revenue.

desk.headline: Revenue up 571% to $981m; 2026 sales now seen at low end of $3.0-3.4bn range, first 2027 outlook $12-13bn
results: Revenue rose 571% to $981m and 68% from Q2, helped by new capacity and about $325m of one-off revenue from the first phase of an asset-light partnership.
The AI cloud unit made almost all of group revenue and earned a 53.2% adjusted EBITDA margin; group adjusted EBITDA was $466m.
The GAAP net loss narrowed to $37.5m ($0.13 a share), after $354.7m of depreciation, $112.5m of interest and a $49.5m charge on converting notes.
Capex hit $7.3bn in the quarter; customer prepayments lifted deferred revenue to about $9.4bn, while debt rose to about $14.2bn.
Annualised run-rate revenue reached $6.4bn at end-September, but the company says it will stop using ARR as a key measure.

guidance.summary: Nebius now expects 2026 revenue at the low end of its $3.0-3.4bn range as some sales slip into early 2027, with an adjusted EBITDA margin of about 40%; the ARR level targeted for December is now expected in February. Its first 2027 outlook calls for $12-13bn of revenue, $40-45bn of capex and pre-tax breakeven by end-2027.

points: Prepayments on Q3 deals covered more than 100% of the related capex, up from 50-60% in Q2, and the trend continued into Q4.
Contract pricing improved: annual contract value per MW topped $25m and GPU-hour prices rose over 20% versus Q2; payback shortened to 1 year 7 months.
Customers committed over $12bn of contract value since the start of Q3, with Databricks, Datadog and Snowflake among first enterprise deals.
Third-party colocation sites slipped into H1 2027, including the remaining New Jersey tranches for Microsoft, now due in Q2 2027.
Prepayments and asset-backed financing are expected to fund 75-85% of 2027 capex; from 2027 guidance will cover revenue and pre-tax earnings.

watch: Whether delayed colocation capacity, especially New Jersey, comes online on the new timetable.
How much of the $40-45bn 2027 capex is funded by prepayments versus new debt or equity.
Whether asset-light partnership revenue becomes recurring after the one-off $325m in Q3.
